cohort: The study included 97 female patients with Moyamoya disease who underwent either vaginal delivery or cesarean section, identified from the National Inpatient Sample database.
finding: The study did not find evidence that vaginal delivery and cesarean section are independent risk factors for arterial ischemic stroke in pregnant patients with Moyamoya disease.
mod_finding: A higher prevalence of AIS was observed after vaginal delivery compared with C-section (8.2% vs 6.3%), but multivariate analysis did not find vaginal delivery to be an independent risk factor for AIS compared to C-section.
